library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

Tang 2026 reports the exposure-response analyses supporting the datopotamab
deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) dose of 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks, capped at 540 mg for
patients weighing 90 kg or more. It fits **two Cox proportional-hazards models**
for efficacy in hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer
(TROPION-Breast01, n = 352) and **eight logistic-regression models** for safety
in a pooled breast and lung cancer population (n = 1081, four studies). A ninth
and tenth safety endpoint (adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease and
TEAE leading to treatment discontinuation) showed no exposure-response
relationship and were not modelled further. All ten fitted models are packaged;
this vignette walks the paper as a unit.

```{r models}
erModels <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Model,                                       ~Endpoint,                                 ~`Exposure metric`,         ~Output,
  "Tang_2026_datopotamab_os",                   "Overall survival",                        "Dato-DXd AUC1",            "hr",
  "Tang_2026_datopotamab_pfs",                  "Progression-free survival",               "none (tumor size only)",   "hr",
  "Tang_2026_datopotamab_teae_grade3",          "Grade 3+ TEAE",                           "DXd Cavg (ng/mL)",         "prob_teae_grade3",
  "Tang_2026_datopotamab_sae",                  "Serious TEAE",                            "DXd Cavg (ng/mL)",         "prob_sae",
  "Tang_2026_datopotamab_dose_interruption",    "TEAE leading to dose interruption",       "Dato-DXd AUC1",            "prob_dose_interruption",
  "Tang_2026_datopotamab_dose_reduction",       "TEAE leading to dose reduction",          "Dato-DXd AUC1",            "prob_dose_reduction",
  "Tang_2026_datopotamab_stomatitis",           "Any-grade stomatitis",                    "Dato-DXd Cavg (ug/mL)",    "prob_stomatitis",
  "Tang_2026_datopotamab_stomatitis_grade2",    "Grade 2+ stomatitis",                     "Dato-DXd AUC1",            "prob_stomatitis_grade2",
  "Tang_2026_datopotamab_ose",                  "Any-grade ocular surface event",          "Dato-DXd Cavg (ug/mL)",    "prob_ocular_surface_event",
  "Tang_2026_datopotamab_ose_grade2",           "Grade 2+ ocular surface event",           "Dato-DXd Cavg (ug/mL)",    "prob_ocular_surface_event_grade2"
)
knitr::kable(erModels, caption = "The ten packaged Tang 2026 models. AUC1 is in ug*day/mL.")
```

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tang_2026_datopotamab_os"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.70188> (open access, PMC13084299)
* The individual exposures were empirical Bayes predictions from the population
  PK model of Hong 2025, packaged as `Hong_2025_datopotamab`; that model is used
  below to regenerate the Cycle-1 AUC distribution.

None of the ten models has an ODE or a dose: the exposure metric is a data
column. AUC1 (`AUC_DATODXD`) is the Cycle-1 (day 0-21) AUC of intact Dato-DXd.
Cavg (`CAV`) is the cumulative AUC divided by the time from the first dose to
the end of the cycle of the event (or of the last treatment for patients without
an event), so it is endpoint-specific. **`CAV` carries two different analytes**:
the released payload DXd in ng/mL for the grade 3+ TEAE and serious TEAE models,
and intact Dato-DXd in ug/mL for the stomatitis and ocular-surface-event models.

# Population

```{r population}
pop <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Characteristic,             ~`Efficacy set (TROPION-Breast01)`, ~`Safety set (4 studies)`,
  "N",                         "352",                               "1081",
  "Age, median (range), y",    "55 (29-86)",                        "60 (26-86)",
  "Weight, median (range), kg", "62 (35.6-141)",                    "64.2 (35.6-156)",
  "Female",                    "98.6%",                             "67.2%",
  "White",                     "50%",                               "47.2%",
  "Tumour type",               "HR+/HER2- breast cancer",           "59.5% NSCLC, 36.4% HR+/HER2- BC, 4.1% TNBC",
  "Dose",                      "6 mg/kg Q3W",                       "0.27-10 mg/kg Q3W (85% at 6 mg/kg)",
  "Baseline albumin, median",  "41 g/L",                            "39 g/L",
  "Baseline tumor size, median", "55 mm",                           "60 mm"
)
knitr::kable(pop, caption = "Tang 2026 Results (Baseline Characteristics) and Table S2.")
```

The safety set pools TROPION-PanTumor01 (phase 1, 0.27-10 mg/kg; 295 patients),
TROPION-Lung05 (137), TROPION-Lung01 (297) and TROPION-Breast01 (352); data
cut-off 29 April 2024. TEAE leading to dose interruption was analysed only in
TROPION-PanTumor01 and TROPION-Breast01. Regions: USA 29.7%, Europe 27.8%,
Japan 17.8%, mainland China 4.5%, rest of world 20.2%.

# Source trace

| Model | Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| os | log-HR per ug*day/mL AUC1 | -0.0031 | Results, OS equation |
| pfs | log-HR per median-normalised tumor size | 0.28 | Results, PFS equation; Methods CPH equation |
| pfs | tumor-size median | 55 mm | Results ('median tumor size of 55 mm') |
| teae_grade3 | intercept; DXd Cavg; Japan; Europe; China; rest of world; ever-smoker | -1.1706039; 1.3054368; -0.6327399; -0.3466507; -0.3995153; -0.7647521; 0.4538759 | Table S4, TEAE Gr3+ |
| sae | intercept; DXd Cavg; albumin; breast cancer; Black; Asian; multiple/other; unknown | 1.361896; 1.382566; -2.94387; -0.86092; -0.2853; -0.85655; -0.59128; 0.039894 | Table S4, Serious AE |
| sae | albumin median | 39 g/L | Results ('median albumin level (39 g/L)') |
| dose_interruption | intercept; AUC1 | -2.73329; 0.002195 | Table S4, Dose Interruption |
| dose_reduction | intercept; AUC1; tumor size | -2.70582; 0.002585; -0.40425 | Table S4, Dose Reduction |
| dose_reduction | tumor-size median | 60 mm | Results ('median tumor size baseline (60 mm)') |
| stomatitis | intercept; Dato-DXd Cavg | -2.35939; 0.07587 | Table S4, Stomatitis Any Grade |
| stomatitis_grade2 | intercept; AUC1 | -2.92847; 0.00288 | Table S4, Stomatitis Grade 2+ |
| ose | intercept; Dato-DXd Cavg; breast cancer | -3.67083; 0.074398; 1.040719 | Table S4, OSE Any Grade |
| ose_grade2 | intercept; Dato-DXd Cavg | -4.74822; 0.070107 | Table S4, OSE Grade 2+ |
| all logistic | link: P = 1 / (1 + exp(-(theta + theta_i x_i + theta_j x_j / x_median + theta_k PK))) | -- | Methods, Exposure-Safety Analysis |
| os, pfs | h(t) = h0(t) exp(theta_i x_i + theta_j x_j / x_median + theta_k PK) | -- | Methods, Exposure-Efficacy Analysis |

The two equations in the last rows fix the covariate scaling: binary covariates
enter as indicators, continuous non-exposure covariates are divided by their
cohort median, and the exposure metric enters linearly and uncentred.

# Structural checks: hazard and odds ratios

The Results and Figures 1 and 3 print hazard and odds ratios at named covariate
values. Each packaged model is solved at the two values and the ratio is compared
with the printed one. This exercises the median normalisations inside `model()`:
reading the PFS tumor-size coefficient per mm instead of per median would move
its hazard ratio by ten orders of magnitude.

```{r solve_helper}
# The models are algebraic -- no ODE, no dose, no time dimension -- so a grid of
# covariate values is swept along a dummy `time` axis for one subject. Scalars
# are recycled to the grid length.
solveStatic <- function(modelName, covs) {
  n <- max(vapply(covs, length, integer(1)))
  ev <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq_len(n), amt = 0, evid = 0L)
  for (nm in names(covs)) ev[[nm]] <- rep_len(covs[[nm]], n)
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(modelName)),
    events = ev, returnType = "data.frame"
  ))
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == n)
  s
}

hazardRatio <- function(modelName, covName, value, ref, extra = list()) {
  h <- solveStatic(modelName, c(setNames(list(c(ref, value)), covName), extra))$hr
  h[2] / h[1]
}
oddsRatio <- function(modelName, output, covName, value, ref, extra = list()) {
  p <- solveStatic(modelName, c(setNames(list(c(ref, value)), covName), extra))[[output]]
  (p[2] / (1 - p[2])) / (p[1] / (1 - p[1]))
}

saeBase <- list(CAV = 0.7, ALB = 39, TUMTP_BREAST = 0, RACE_BLACK = 0, RACE_ASIAN = 0,
                RACE_OTHER = 0, RACE_MISSING = 0)
teaeBase <- list(CAV = 0.7, REGION_JAPAN = 0, REGION_EUROPE = 0, REGION_CHINA = 0,
                 REGION_ROW = 0, SMOKE_NEVER = 1)

ratioCheck <- tibble::tribble(

  "Grade 3+ TEAE: rest of world vs USA (OR)",    oddsRatio("Tang_2026_datopotamab_teae_grade3", "prob_teae_grade3", "REGION_ROW", 1, 0, teaeBase[-5]),  0.465, "Results / Fig S4A",
  "Grade 3+ TEAE: China vs USA (OR)",            oddsRatio("Tang_2026_datopotamab_teae_grade3", "prob_teae_grade3", "REGION_CHINA", 1, 0, teaeBase[-4]), 0.671, "Results / Fig S4A",

  mutate(`% difference` = 100 * (Recovered - Published) / Published)

knitr::kable(ratioCheck, digits = 3,

```

```{r ratio_assertions}
# Deterministic: each ratio is an exact function of the packaged coefficients, so
# the only discrepancy is the rounding of the printed ratio and of the printed
# covariate percentiles (138, 17, 46, 29, 166 and 18 are themselves rounded).
# The largest observed difference is about 0.6% (SAE breast vs lung: the Table S4
# coefficient gives 0.423 against the printed 0.425); 1% covers rounding and
# nothing else.
stopifnot(all(abs(ratioCheck$`% difference`) < 1))
```

# Cycle-1 exposure regenerated from Hong 2025

The exposure metrics were empirical Bayes predictions from the Hong 2025
population PK model, which is packaged. Simulating a TROPION-Breast01-like
cohort through it and computing the Cycle-1 AUC with PKNCA reproduces the
exposure scale that the AUC1-driven models were fitted on, and gives the
4 and 8 mg/kg exposures needed for the dose projections further down.

## Virtual cohort

Covariates follow the TROPION-Breast01 column of Tang 2026 Table S2: body weight
median 62 kg (IQR 54.9-72.7), 98.6% female, age 55.4 +/- 11.7 years, albumin
median 41 g/L (IQR 38-44), AST median 34.1 U/L (IQR 24.1-57.5), total bilirubin
median 0.48 mg/dL (IQR 0.345-0.645), tumor size median 55 mm (IQR 36.8-85.3) and
the study's region mix. Log-normal spreads are set from the IQRs. Hong 2025 has
no separate China level for DXd clearance, so mainland China is coded as rest of
world for that model, as Hong 2025 did.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260416)
nPerArm <- 200
makeArm <- function(doseMgKg, idOffset) {
  wt <- pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(nPerArm, log(62), (log(72.7) - log(54.9)) / 1.349)), 35.6), 141)
  region <- sample(c("Japan", "USA", "Europe", "China", "RoW"), nPerArm, replace = TRUE,
                   prob = c(30, 32, 134, 44, 112))
  data.frame(
    id = idOffset + seq_len(nPerArm),
    WT = wt,
    AGE = pmin(pmax(rnorm(nPerArm, 55.4, 11.7), 29), 86),
    SEXF = rbinom(nPerArm, 1, 0.986),
    ALB = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(nPerArm, log(41), (log(44) - log(38)) / 1.349)), 24), 75.4),
    AST = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(nPerArm, log(34.1), (log(57.5) - log(24.1)) / 1.349)), 11), 223),
    TBILI = 17.1 * pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(nPerArm, log(0.48), (log(0.645) - log(0.345)) / 1.349)), 0.17), 3.32),
    TUMSZ = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(nPerArm, log(55), (log(85.3) - log(36.8)) / 1.349)), 10), 338),
    REGION_JAPAN = as.integer(region == "Japan"),
    REGION_EUROPE = as.integer(region == "Europe"),
    REGION_ROW = as.integer(region %in% c("RoW", "China")),
    CYCLE = 1L,
    amtMg = doseMgKg * wt,
    treatment = paste(doseMgKg, "mg/kg")
  )
}
cohort <- bind_rows(makeArm(4, 0), makeArm(6, 1000), makeArm(8, 2000))
knitr::kable(
  cohort |>
    group_by(treatment) |>
    summarise(N = n(), `Median WT (kg)` = median(WT), `Female (%)` = 100 * mean(SEXF),
              `Median dose (mg)` = median(amtMg), .groups = "drop"),
  digits = 1, caption = "Virtual cohort, one arm per dose level."
)
```

## Simulation

One Cycle-1 dose, observed to day 21. Hong 2025 declares two endpoints (Dato-DXd
and DXd), so observation rows name the central ODE state and carry `dvid = 1`
(the Dato-DXd endpoint); rxode2 returns both concentration columns on every row.

```{r simulate}
obsTimes <- c(0, 0.0625, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 10, 14, 17, 21)
covCols <- setdiff(names(cohort), c("id", "amtMg", "treatment"))
events <- bind_rows(
  cohort |> transmute(id, time = 0, amt = amtMg, evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_),
  tidyr::crossing(id = cohort$id, time = obsTimes) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
) |>
  left_join(cohort[, c("id", covCols)], by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

simPk <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hong_2025_datopotamab")), events,
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  left_join(cohort[, c("id", "treatment", "amtMg")], by = "id")
stopifnot(length(unique(simPk$id)) == nrow(cohort))
```

```{r pk_profile, fig.height = 4}
simPk |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(median = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, median, colour = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (day)", y = "Dato-DXd concentration (ug/mL)",
       title = "Cycle-1 Dato-DXd profiles from Hong_2025_datopotamab",
       subtitle = "Median and 90% prediction interval, TROPION-Breast01-like cohort") +
  theme_bw()
```

## PKNCA

```{r pknca}
# Filter on !is.na(Cc) only: the grid includes time 0, which PKNCA needs as the
# start of the 0-21 day interval.
concData <- simPk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
stopifnot(all(tapply(concData$time, concData$id, min) == 0))
doseData <- cohort |> transmute(id, treatment, time = 0, amtMg)

concObj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(concData, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
doseObj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doseData, amtMg ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 21, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE)
ncaRes <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(concObj, doseObj, intervals = intervals))
ncaInd <- as.data.frame(ncaRes)
auc1 <- ncaInd |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, treatment, AUC_DATODXD = PPORRES)
stopifnot(nrow(auc1) == nrow(cohort), !any(is.na(auc1$AUC_DATODXD)))
```

## Comparison against the published exposure

Tang 2026 prints the TROPION-Breast01 AUC1 median (650 ug*day/mL) and its 5th and
95th percentiles (467 and 864 ug*day/mL) at 6 mg/kg. Figure 2C marks the pooled
safety-set medians at 4, 6 and 8 mg/kg; read from the figure they are about 380,
650 and 920 ug*day/mL (maintainers' reading of the dashed lines, +/- about 15).

```{r nca_comparison}
simulatedSummary <- auc1 |>
  filter(treatment == "6 mg/kg") |>
  summarise(median = median(AUC_DATODXD), p05 = quantile(AUC_DATODXD, 0.05),
            p95 = quantile(AUC_DATODXD, 0.95))

simulatedLong <- auc1 |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(PPORRES = median(AUC_DATODXD), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(PPTESTCD = "auclast")
published <- data.frame(treatment = c("4 mg/kg", "6 mg/kg", "8 mg/kg"),
                        auclast = c(380, 650, 920))

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = simulatedLong, reference = published, by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "ug*day/mL"), tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Median Cycle-1 Dato-DXd AUC (day 0-21): Hong 2025 simulation versus Tang 2026.",
    "The 6 mg/kg reference is the printed TROPION-Breast01 median; 4 and 8 mg/kg are read from Figure 2C."
  ))

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(Statistic = c("5th percentile", "median", "95th percentile"),
             Published = c(467, 650, 864),
             Simulated = unlist(simulatedSummary[c("p05", "median", "p95")])),
  digits = 0, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "TROPION-Breast01 AUC1 distribution at 6 mg/kg (ug*day/mL)."
)
```

```{r nca_assertions}
med6 <- simulatedSummary$median
# The simulated median sits a few percent above the printed 650 on the runs used
# to write this check (about +5%). A mis-transcribed Hong 2025 clearance, a unit
# slip or dosing in mg instead of mg/kg moves it by tens of percent. The tails
# are wider than the published empirical-Bayes tails (shrinkage narrows the
# latter), so only the centre is asserted.
stopifnot(abs(100 * (med6 - 650) / 650) < 12)
# Exposure rises more than proportionally with dose (Michaelis-Menten
# elimination), as Figure 2C shows: the 8 mg/kg median is more than 4/3 of the
# 6 mg/kg median and the 4 mg/kg median less than 2/3 of it.
medByDose <- setNames(simulatedLong$PPORRES, simulatedLong$treatment)
stopifnot(medByDose[["8 mg/kg"]] / medByDose[["6 mg/kg"]] > 4 / 3,
          medByDose[["4 mg/kg"]] / medByDose[["6 mg/kg"]] < 2 / 3)
```

# Exposure-safety curves (Figure 2)

Figure 2 shows four of the eight logistic models against their exposure metric.
The curves below are the packaged models with every covariate at its reference
level (USA, never-smoker for grade 3+ TEAE; White, lung cancer, median albumin
for serious TEAE). The vertical lines are the dose-level exposure medians read
from Figure 2.

```{r fig2, fig.height = 6}
fig2Medians <- tibble::tribble(
  ~panel,                         ~dose,     ~x,
  "(a) Grade 3+ TEAE",            "4 mg/kg", 0.56,
  "(a) Grade 3+ TEAE",            "6 mg/kg", 0.77,
  "(a) Grade 3+ TEAE",            "8 mg/kg", 1.15,
  "(b) Serious TEAE",             "4 mg/kg", 0.56,
  "(b) Serious TEAE",             "6 mg/kg", 0.77,
  "(b) Serious TEAE",             "8 mg/kg", 1.15,
  "(c) Grade 2+ stomatitis",      "4 mg/kg", 380,
  "(c) Grade 2+ stomatitis",      "6 mg/kg", 650,
  "(c) Grade 2+ stomatitis",      "8 mg/kg", 920,
  "(d) Grade 2+ OSE",             "4 mg/kg", 22.3,
  "(d) Grade 2+ OSE",             "6 mg/kg", 31.4,
  "(d) Grade 2+ OSE",             "8 mg/kg", 42.4
)

dxdGrid <- seq(0, 1.4, length.out = 60)
aucGrid <- seq(0, 1300, length.out = 60)
cavGrid <- seq(0, 62, length.out = 60)
fig2Curves <- bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(panel = "(a) Grade 3+ TEAE", x = dxdGrid,
                 p = solveStatic("Tang_2026_datopotamab_teae_grade3", c(list(CAV = dxdGrid), teaeBase[-1]))$prob_teae_grade3),
  tibble::tibble(panel = "(b) Serious TEAE", x = dxdGrid,
                 p = solveStatic("Tang_2026_datopotamab_sae", c(list(CAV = dxdGrid), saeBase[-1]))$prob_sae),
  tibble::tibble(panel = "(c) Grade 2+ stomatitis", x = aucGrid,
                 p = solveStatic("Tang_2026_datopotamab_stomatitis_grade2", list(AUC_DATODXD = aucGrid))$prob_stomatitis_grade2),
  tibble::tibble(panel = "(d) Grade 2+ OSE", x = cavGrid,
                 p = solveStatic("Tang_2026_datopotamab_ose_grade2", list(CAV = cavGrid))$prob_ocular_surface_event_grade2)
)

ggplot(fig2Curves, aes(x, p)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(data = fig2Medians, aes(xintercept = x, colour = dose), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Exposure: DXd Cavg (ng/mL) in a-b; Dato-DXd AUC1 (ug*day/mL) in c; Dato-DXd Cavg (ug/mL) in d",
       y = "Predicted event probability", colour = NULL,
       title = "Replicates Figure 2 of Tang 2026") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Panels (c) and (d) have no covariate other than exposure, so they are directly
comparable with the published curves. Through the middle of the data they agree
(for example 23% at an AUC1 of 600 ug*day/mL and 16% at a Dato-DXd Cavg of
44 ug/mL, as plotted), but the published curves are steeper at the extremes:
read at the right edge, Figure 2C reaches about 77% at 1300 ug*day/mL against
69% from the Table S4 coefficients, and Figure 2D about 46% at 62 ug/mL against
40%. The printed dose projections below side with Table S4, so the packaged
values follow the table; see Assumptions and deviations.

# Dose projections

Tang 2026 projects grade 3+ TEAE rates of 33.3%, 39.5% and 51.3% at 4, 6 and
8 mg/kg, and grade 2+ OSE increases of 3.3 and 7 percentage points from 4 to 6
and from 6 to 8 mg/kg, using "the median PopPK-predicted PK metric values at
each dose level". The paper does not say at which covariate values the grade 3+
TEAE projection was made, so that check anchors on the printed 6 mg/kg rate and
tests only the exposure slope, which is covariate-independent on the logit
scale.

```{r projections}
logit <- function(p) log(p / (1 - p))
expit <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))
dxdMed <- c(`4 mg/kg` = 0.56, `6 mg/kg` = 0.77, `8 mg/kg` = 1.15)   # Figure 2A dashed lines
oseMed <- c(`4 mg/kg` = 22.3, `6 mg/kg` = 31.4, `8 mg/kg` = 42.4)   # Figure 2D dashed lines

teae <- solveStatic("Tang_2026_datopotamab_teae_grade3", c(list(CAV = dxdMed), teaeBase[-1]))$prob_teae_grade3
# Shift the reference-level logits so the 6 mg/kg value equals the printed 39.5%.
offset <- logit(0.395) - logit(teae[2])
teaeProj <- 100 * expit(logit(teae) + offset)

ose <- 100 * solveStatic("Tang_2026_datopotamab_ose_grade2", list(CAV = oseMed))$prob_ocular_surface_event_grade2

projCheck <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Quantity,                                  ~Model,                   ~Published,
  "Grade 3+ TEAE at 4 mg/kg (%)",             teaeProj[1],              33.3,
  "Grade 3+ TEAE at 8 mg/kg (%)",             teaeProj[3],              51.3,
  "Grade 2+ OSE increase, 4 to 6 mg/kg (points)", ose[2] - ose[1],      3.3,
  "Grade 2+ OSE increase, 6 to 8 mg/kg (points)", ose[3] - ose[2],      7
)
knitr::kable(projCheck, digits = 1, caption = "Dose projections reproduced from the packaged models and the Figure 2 exposure medians.")
```

```{r projection_assertions}
# The exposure medians are read from Figure 2 to about +/- 0.02 ng/mL and
# +/- 0.5 ug/mL, which moves these projections by up to about 1 percentage
# point; 2 points covers that. A slope taken from the steeper published curves
# instead of Table S4 (about 1.7 instead of 1.305 per ng/mL for grade 3+ TEAE)
# misses the 4 and 8 mg/kg values by 2 and 4 points.
stopifnot(all(abs(projCheck$Model - projCheck$Published) < 2))
```

The stated increase in TEAE leading to dose reduction (7 points from 4 to
6 mg/kg, 14 from 6 to 8) is not used as a check because the 4 mg/kg AUC1 median
cannot be read from Figure 2C precisely enough: at the median tumor size the
model gives `r round(100 * diff(solveStatic("Tang_2026_datopotamab_dose_reduction", list(AUC_DATODXD = c(380, 650, 920), TUMSZ = 60))$prob_dose_reduction), 1)`
points over the two steps.

# Predicted versus observed incidence

The AUC1-driven models can be pushed through the simulated exposures to give a
cohort-averaged incidence at each dose level, which Table 2 reports as observed
incidences. The simulated cohort is TROPION-Breast01-like while the 4 and
8 mg/kg patients in the paper came mostly from TROPION-PanTumor01, so this is a
plausibility check, not a validation target.

```{r observed}
aucCohort <- auc1 |> left_join(cohort[, c("id", "TUMSZ")], by = "id")
predByDose <- aucCohort |>
  mutate(
    stom2 = solveStatic("Tang_2026_datopotamab_stomatitis_grade2", list(AUC_DATODXD = AUC_DATODXD))$prob_stomatitis_grade2,
    interr = solveStatic("Tang_2026_datopotamab_dose_interruption", list(AUC_DATODXD = AUC_DATODXD))$prob_dose_interruption,
    reduc = solveStatic("Tang_2026_datopotamab_dose_reduction", list(AUC_DATODXD = AUC_DATODXD, TUMSZ = TUMSZ))$prob_dose_reduction
  ) |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(across(c(stom2, interr, reduc), ~ 100 * mean(.x)), .groups = "drop")

obsTable2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~stom2_obs, ~interr_obs, ~reduc_obs,
  "4 mg/kg",  8,          8,           2,
  "6 mg/kg",  29,         24,          21,
  "8 mg/kg",  34,         35,          28
)
predByDose |>
  left_join(obsTable2, by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose" = treatment,
                "Grade 2+ stomatitis, predicted (%)" = stom2, "Grade 2+ stomatitis, observed (%)" = stom2_obs,
                "Dose interruption, predicted (%)" = interr, "Dose interruption, observed (%)" = interr_obs,
                "Dose reduction, predicted (%)" = reduc, "Dose reduction, observed (%)" = reduc_obs) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Cohort-averaged predictions versus Tang 2026 Table 2 observed incidences.")
```

At 6 mg/kg, where 85% of the safety set was treated, the predictions sit within
a few points of the observed rates. The 4 mg/kg arm (n = 50) is small and the
observed rates there are noisy.

# Exposure-efficacy (Figure 1)

The overall-survival model is a pure exposure-hazard relationship; its hazard
ratios across the TROPION-Breast01 AUC1 quartile medians (Table S5) show the
size of the association the paper reports.

```{r efficacy}
quartileMedians <- c(Q1 = 519, Q2 = 607, Q3 = 688, Q4 = 779)
osHr <- solveStatic("Tang_2026_datopotamab_os", list(AUC_DATODXD = c(650, quartileMedians)))$hr
tumorGrid <- c(17, 36.8, 55, 85.3, 138)
pfsHr <- solveStatic("Tang_2026_datopotamab_pfs", list(TUMSZ = tumorGrid))$hr

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(`AUC1 quartile` = names(quartileMedians), `Median AUC1 (ug*day/mL)` = quartileMedians,
             `OS hazard ratio vs 650` = osHr[-1] / osHr[1], check.names = FALSE),
  digits = 3, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Overall-survival hazard ratios at the Table S5 AUC1 quartile medians."
)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(`Baseline tumor size (mm)` = tumorGrid, `PFS hazard ratio vs 55 mm` = pfsHr / pfsHr[3],
             check.names = FALSE),
  digits = 3, caption = "Progression-free-survival hazard ratios across the TROPION-Breast01 tumor-size distribution (5th, 25th, 50th, 75th, 95th percentiles)."
)
```

The Cox models carry no baseline hazard, so they cannot reproduce the
Kaplan-Meier curves of Figure 1A-D; only the hazard ratios of Figure 1E-F are
model outputs.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **No baseline hazard.** Both Cox models are semiparametric; h0(t) is not a
  parameter of the fit, so the models return the relative hazard `hr` (and its
  log, `lhr`) only. Only ratios of `hr` between two covariate settings are
  meaningful.
* **PFS model has no exposure term.** Dato-DXd AUC1 entered the progression-free
  survival model in forward addition and was removed in backward elimination
  (p = 0.0011 against the p < 0.001 criterion); the packaged model is the final
  model, with baseline tumor size only.
* **PFS coefficient precision.** The coefficient is printed as 0.28. The two
  published hazard ratios back-solve to 0.2775 and 0.2784, both of which round to
  0.28; the printed value is used.
* **Median normalisation.** The Methods equations divide each continuous
  non-exposure covariate by its median; the medians used (55 mm for PFS tumor
  size, 39 g/L for SAE albumin, 60 mm for dose-reduction tumor size) are the
  values the Results quote as the reference of each forest plot. The
  printed hazard and odds ratios reproduce to within 1% only under this reading.
* **Figure 2 curves versus Table S4.** The plotted curves of Figure 2C and 2D,
  whose models have no covariates, are steeper at the extremes than the Table S4
  coefficients (about 77% versus 69% at 1300 ug*day/mL AUC1; 46% versus 40% at
  62 ug/mL Cavg). The printed dose projections for grade 3+ TEAE and grade 2+ OSE
  reproduce with the Table S4 slopes and not with the steeper plotted ones, so
  the packaged values are the Table S4 estimates, unchanged.
* **Two analytes under `CAV`.** The grade 3+ TEAE and serious TEAE models are
  driven by the DXd payload Cavg in ng/mL; the stomatitis and OSE models by the
  intact Dato-DXd Cavg in ug/mL. Each model's `covariateData` states the unit.
  `Hong_2025_datopotamab` returns both analytes in ug/mL (`Cc`, `Cc_dxd`), so
  DXd must be multiplied by 1000.
* **Cavg is endpoint-specific.** Its averaging window ends at the cycle of the
  event, so it cannot be regenerated from a fixed simulation horizon. The
  vignette uses the dose-level medians read from Figure 2 instead.
* **Race levels.** Table S4 gives coefficients for Black, Asian, "Multiple or
  Other" and "Unknown or Unreported" versus White. The two patients recorded as
  American Indian or Alaska Native or Native Hawaiian or other Pacific Islander
  and the 8 with race missing are not assigned to a level by the paper.
  "Multiple or Other" is carried as `RACE_OTHER` and "Unknown or Unreported" as
  `RACE_MISSING`.
* **Smoking.** The paper contrasts former or current smokers with never smokers;
  the model forms the ever-smoker indicator as `1 - SMOKE_NEVER`.
* **Region.** The grade 3+ TEAE model's reference region is the USA, with
  separate Japan, Europe, mainland China and rest-of-world levels. Hong 2025
  pools mainland China into rest of world, and the virtual cohort does the same
  when it drives that PK model.
* **Residual error.** The logistic models were fitted with a Bernoulli
  likelihood and report no variance components. A fixed placeholder additive
  error of 0.001 on each probability exists only because rxode2 needs an
  observation declaration; sample outcomes with `rbinom()` on the predicted
  probability instead.
* **Virtual cohort.** Covariate spreads are log-normal fits to the Table S2
  TROPION-Breast01 medians and IQRs, truncated to the observed ranges; dosing is
  a single 6 mg/kg (or 4, 8 mg/kg) bolus without the 540 mg cap, which was
  introduced after these studies.
